sentences.text: JUDGMENT This claim petition is filed under section 166 of the M.V. Act, seeking compensation for the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident.

2. It is the case of the petitioner that on 29.07.2022 at about 1.30 p.m, when the petitioner was proceeding as occupant in the Hyundai car bearing Reg.No.KA-11-M-3799 and was coming from Gowribidanur to Bengaluru, on Bengaluru - Doddaballapura road, when the said car reached near Gundumgere cross, Doddaballapura Taluk, the driver of the car drove the same in rash and negligent manner and dashed to the opposite coming another Honda City car bearing Reg.No.KA-01- ME-2276 and thereby sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately he was rushed to Government Hospital, Doddaballapura, wherein he took first aid and then he was shifted to Apollo Hospital, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient.
It is specifically urged that, the petitioner has spent Rs.1,00,000/- for his treatment.
It is further submitted that the petitioner was hale and healthy and was studying in Final year Engineering.
It is specifically urged that, due to the said accident he could not able to attend the classes regularly and unable to do his work.
Further it is specifically urged that, the accident happened because of rash and negligent driver of the car driver.
The respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation, as such prayed to grant a compensation amount.
3. Notice was duly served to respondent No.2, the respondent No.2 did not appear before this Tribunal.
Hence he was placed exparte.
4. The respondent No.1 filed written statement admitting the issuance of insurance policy in respect of Hyundai car bearing Reg.No.KA-11-M-3799.
However the liability if any is pleaded to be subject to the terms & conditions of the policy.

This respondent contended that the petition is barred by limitation as the accident took place on 27.09.2022, whereas the petition has been filed on 22.06.2023 i.e., after the lapse of 10 months 24 days from the date of accident.

This respondent specifically contended that the accident occurred only due to the negligence of the driver of the car bearing Reg.No.KA-01- ME-2276 which was driving the same and dashed to the car bearing Reg.No.KA-11-M-3799 in which the petitioner was proceeding.
The accident occurred in the middle of the road and head on collision.
The both the drivers of the car were negligently driving their vehicles and causing the accident.
The driver of the car bearing Reg.No.KA-01-ME-2276 caused the accident and not any actionable negligence of the driver of the insured car.
Without prejudice to the said contention it is averred that the driver of the insured car did not possess valid & effective DL as on the date of accident.
Despite knowing the said fact the owner thereof had handed over its possession to such a driver.
On account of willful breach of the terms and conditions of the policy by the insured, the insurance company is not liable to indemnify him.

Non -compliance of Sec's 134(c),
158(6) of the MV Act, 1988 is pleaded.
Rest of the petition averments are repudiated as false and baseless and it is prayed to dismiss the petition.

5. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues were framed :
ISSUES 1
Whether the petitioner proves that he sustained injuries in a road traffic Rohith.

6. The petitioner examined himself as P.W1.
Ex's.P1 to 8 were marked.
The respondent No.1 did not choose to lead any evidence on its behalf.
7. Heard erudite counsel for the petitioner and respondent No.1 counsel on merits.
Perused the entire materials placed on record.

My answers to the above issues are as follows :-
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.3 : As per final order for the following :
REASONS 8. ISSUE NO.1 : The petitioner has knocked the doors of justice with a relief to grant a compensation of an amount to the tune of Rs.2,00,000/- together.

In order to prove the factum of negligence the petitioner has mainly relied on Ex.P.1 FIR, Ex.P.2 Complaint, Ex.P.3 Spot mahazar, Ex.P.4 Sketch,
Ex.P.5 IMV Report, Ex.P.6 Chargesheet and Ex.P.7 Wound certificate.

The evidence on record reveals that after the receipt of complaint lodged by one Smt. P. Nagarathna, the jurisdictional police conducted thorough investigation and filed charge sheet against the driver of car bearing Reg.No.KA-11-M-3799 for the offences punishable u/s's 279, 337 & 338 of IPC.
There is nothing on record to believe that the charge sheet filed by the police is defective or collusive.
Though the respondent No.1 has denied the cause of the accident, it has not let in any cogent evidence to prove its defence or to disprove the evidence led by the petitioner.
Mere taking of defence is not sufficient to dislodge the testimony of other side, which has no sanctity in the eyes of Law.
Under such circumstances the evidence of PW.1 which is supported by police documents has to be accepted.

Consequently I hold that the accident is proved to have been caused due to the actionable negligence of the driver of car bearing Reg.No.KA-11-M-3799.
9.

The learned counsel for the respondent No.1 vehemently contended that as there is no negligence on the part of the insured car driver and certain degree of negligence must be attributed to the driver of the car bearing Reg.No.KA01-ME- 2276.
As the accident occurred in the middle of the road and head on collision.
The both the drivers of the car were negligently driving their vehicles and causing the accident.
The driver of the car bearing Reg.No.KA-01-ME-2276 caused the accident and not any actionable negligence of the driver of the insured car.
In this regard perusal of the spot sketch it reveals that the accident occurred on the left side of the Doddaballapura - Gowribidanur road.
Further the petitioner stated that they were coming from Gowribidanur to Bengaluru side.

On perusal of the sketch it clearly reveals that the driver of the car bearing Reg.No.KA-11-M-3799 was coming at opposite direction with high speed in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the car bearing Reg.No.KA-01-ME-2276.
Further as per the say of the petitioner in his cross examination the accident had happened because of the negligence on the part of their car driver.

The offending Rohith.T.R vs Bajaj All Gen Ins Co Ltd on 9 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122667589/
3 vehicle has caused accident to the other vehicle on opposite direction.

sentences.text: If the driver of the insured car was coming in a normal speed then he would certainly avoided the accident.
Above all even the charge sheet was also filed as against the driver of the insured car for the offences punishable u/s 279, 337, 338 of IPC.
This court is aware of the fact that charge sheet is not a conclusive proof to come to conclusion with regard to rash and negligent act.
But having regard to the Ex.P.3 & 4 which was read in consonance with the Ex.P.6 Charge sheet it is crystal clear that there is rash and negligent act of the driver of the insured car.
In this view of the matter no iota of negligence can be attributed on the part of the driver of the car bearing Reg.No.KA-01-ME-2276 in the occurrence of resultant accident.

But in the instant case having regard to the other materials placed on record and other surrounding circumstances it is it is clearly forthcoming that the negligence on the part of the driver of the car bearing Reg.No.KA-11-M-3799.
Consequently this tribunal hold that the accident is proved to have been caused due to the actionable negligence of the driver of the car bearing Reg.No.KA-11-M- 3799.

With this observation issue No.1 is answered as 'In the Affirmative'.
10. ISSUE NO.2 :
As already discussed above the petitioner has proved that the accident took place due to the actionable negligence of the driver of car.
Therefore he is entitled for compensation.

11. As per the contents of the wound certificate the petitioner has sustained the following injuries :
(i) A Superficial abrasion present of left side of the forehead about 4x1 cms in length.
It is needless to say that the said injury is simple in nature.
12. The petitioner has deposed that on account of the accidental injuries he has become disabled and has lost his earning capacity.
Further he deposed that he was hale and healthy and was studying in Final year Engineering.
It is specifically urged that, due to the said accident he could not able to attend the classes regularly and unable to do his work.
However he has neither proved his avocation nor his earning capacity.
So also the petitioner has not examined the doctor or produced disability certificate to substantiate the fact that he has become permanently disabled.
Under such circumstances, it cannot be accepted that he has suffered permanent disability.
Therefore he is not entitled for compensation under the head 'Loss of future income due to disability'.
In this case the petitioner has not produced medical bills.
Anyhow because the petitioner has not proved that he has any kind of disability, compensation cannot be awarded under conventional heads.

Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, the line of treatment and the medical expenses incurred by him, this tribunal is of the view that ends of justice would be met if the petitioner is awarded global compensation of Rs.30,000/-.
13. INTEREST & LIABILITY :
Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% p.a, is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.
14. There is no dispute with regard to the issuance of insurance policy and its validity as on the date of accident.

Though the insurance company contended that the insured has violated the terms and conditions of the policy, no evidence is adduced to prove such breach of terms and conditions of the policy by the second respondent.

Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the insurer and respondent No.2 being the owner of the offending car bearing Reg.No.KA-11-M-3799 are jointly and severally Rohith.T.R vs Bajaj All Gen Ins Co Ltd on 9 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122667589/
4 liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioner together with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.

sentences.text: However the respondent No.1 being the insurer is primarily liable to satisfy the award amount together with interest within one month from the date of this order.

Hence this issue is answered as 'Partly in the Affirmative'.
15. ISSUE NO.3 :

In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
ORDER

The petition filed under Section 166 of M.V Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms :
The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.30,000/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire award amount.
Respondent No.1 is directed to deposit the aforesaid award amount together with interest within one month from the date of this order.
After deposit of compensation amount the office is directed to release the entire share with interest of the petitioner through NEFT/RTGS by way of E- payment on proper identification.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw an award accordingly.
